- $h(x)=2\sin(2x+\tfrac{\pi}{3})+1$, so $h(x)=0$ requires $\sin(2x+\tfrac{\pi}{3})=-\tfrac12$. This gives zeros at $x=\tfrac{5\pi}{12}+k\pi$ and $x=\tfrac{3\pi}{4}+k\pi$.
- Consecutive gaps alternate between $\tfrac{\pi}{3}$ and $\tfrac{2\pi}{3}$, so each pair of gaps sums to $\pi$.
- Thirty consecutive zeros span 29 gaps, which is $14\pi$ plus one gap. The smallest choice is $14\pi+\tfrac{\pi}{3}=\tfrac{43\pi}{3}$.
- Explicitly, from $z_0=\tfrac{5\pi}{12}$ to $z_{29}=\tfrac{3\pi}{4}+14\pi$ the span is $14\pi+\tfrac{\pi}{3}$. Starting at the other zero type gives $\tfrac{44\pi}{3}$, which is larger.
- Any interval containing 30 zeros must contain the span from its first to its last zero, so $\tfrac{43\pi}{3}$ is the minimum.

The submitted $15\pi\approx 47.12$ is larger than $\tfrac{43\pi}{3}\approx 45.03$. It is achieved by a non-minimal interval, not the minimum. The independent program's check also flagged this.
